about: The prayer begins by asking God to remember His servants and handmaids. The priest then joins his hands and prays in silence for those he intends to name. The prayer then embraces all who are present and names its intentions: the redemption of their souls, the hope of salvation, and their well-being.

s01.translation: Remember, O Lord, Your servants, both men and women

s02.narrative: The priest joins his hands and prays a while in silence for those he means to remember, then spreads his hands and goes on.

s03.translation: and all who are here present, whose faith is known to You and whose devotion is clear to You; for them we offer You

s04.translation: — or they themselves offer You — this sacrifice of praise for themselves and all their own: for the redemption of their souls, in hope of their salvation and well-being;

s05.translation: and fulfill their vows to You, the eternal, living, and true God.

w027.explanation: “A sacrifice of praise” takes up the biblical call to thanksgiving in Psalms 49:14 and 106:22.

w043.explanation: “To render vows” takes up the psalmist's resolve faithfully to fulfill what was promised to the Lord (Ps 115:14, 18).

w047.explanation: The title “the living and true God” echoes 1 Thessalonians 1:9.
